title: Pushforward on global derived Hom for small ringed sites
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O_{\mathcal C})$ and $(\mathcal D,\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})$ be small ringed sites with sheaves of commutative rings. Let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O_{\mathcal C})\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})$ be any morphism of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]; it need not be induced by a functor between the sites, and no final objects are required. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $Rf_*$ for the right derived module direct image, computed by K-injective resolutions [def-pur-kinjective-complex], and $H_Z=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_Z}$ for internal derived Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], for $Z=\mathcal C,\mathcal D$. Derived tensor means the total sheaf tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] computed with K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex]. For a commutative ring $A$ with a specified homomorphism $A\to\Gamma(\mathcal D,\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})$, give all source global sections their induced $A$-action through $\Gamma(\mathcal D,\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})\to\Gamma(\mathcal D,f_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal C})=\Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal O_{\mathcal C})$, the map induced by the structural ring map of $f$. Put $G_Z=R\Gamma(Z,-)$, the right derived global sections functor [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology] restricted to $A$, and $\mathsf H_Z(K,L)=G_ZH_Z(K,L)\in D(A)$.

For all $K,L\in D(\mathcal O_{\mathcal C})$, there is a canonical morphism in $D(A)$, natural contravariantly in $K$ and covariantly in $L$,
$$c_{f;K,L}:\mathsf H_{\mathcal C}(K,L)\longrightarrow\mathsf H_{\mathcal D}(Rf_*K,Rf_*L).$$
More precisely, the canonical unbounded Leray isomorphism is $\lambda_E:G_{\mathcal D}Rf_*E\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{\mathcal C}E$. The internal comparison $\theta_{K,L}:Rf_*H_{\mathcal C}(K,L)\to H_{\mathcal D}(Rf_*K,Rf_*L)$ is the tensor-Hom transpose of relative cup product followed by $Rf_*$ of evaluation,
$$Rf_*H_{\mathcal C}(K,L)\otimes^{\mathbf L}Rf_*K\longrightarrow Rf_*(H_{\mathcal C}(K,L)\otimes^{\mathbf L}K)\longrightarrow Rf_*L.$$
The morphism $c_{f;K,L}$ is $G_{\mathcal D}(\theta_{K,L})\circ\lambda_{H_{\mathcal C}(K,L)}^{-1}$. Under the canonical identifications $H^j\mathsf H_Z(K',L')=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_Z)}(K',L'[j])$, natural in both arguments, its degree-$j$ map sends $v:K\to L[j]$ to $Rf_*v:Rf_*K\to Rf_*(L[j])\cong(Rf_*L)[j]$, using the canonical shift comparison. No quasi-coherence, boundedness, flatness, or invertibility of $c_{f;K,L}$ is assumed or asserted.

proof.text: Put $T=Lf^*$ and $R=Rf_*$. The ordinary module adjunction, the existence of K-flat derived pullback, and K-injective resolutions give the canonical derived adjunction $T\dashv R$. Use the representative-normalized bijection of lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general, not an arbitrary adjunction on isomorphic functors. Write $\varepsilon:TR\to\mathrm{id}$ for its counit and $t_{U,V}:T(U\otimes^{\mathbf L}V)\xrightarrow{\sim}TU\otimes^{\mathbf L}TV$ for the canonical derived tensor comparison. All these results apply to the supplied geometric morphism of topoi; none requires a site functor, a terminal site object, or flatness of the structure map.

For $U,V\in D(\mathcal O_{\mathcal C})$, define $\mu_{U,V}:RU\otimes^{\mathbf L}RV\to R(U\otimes^{\mathbf L}V)$ as the adjunct of $(\varepsilon_U\otimes\varepsilon_V)t_{RU,RV}$. This is precisely the relative cup product: its definition gives
$$\varepsilon_{U\otimes V}T(\mu_{U,V})=(\varepsilon_U\otimes\varepsilon_V)t_{RU,RV}.$$
Set $E=H_{\mathcal C}(K,L)$ and let $e:E\otimes^{\mathbf L}K\to L$ be evaluation. The closed adjunction on $\mathcal D$ transposes $R(e)\mu_{E,K}$ to a unique $\theta_{K,L}:RE\to H_{\mathcal D}(RK,RL)$. Naturality follows from naturality of $t$, $\varepsilon$, and the two adjunction bijections. Explicitly, for $a:K'\to K$ and $b:L\to L'$, the equation $e_{K',L'}(H(a,b)\otimes1)=b\,e_{K,L}(1\otimes a)$ implies the required naturality equation after applying $R$, the naturality of $\mu$, and the injective transpose bijection. Thus both variances are as asserted.

Present the punctual topos by its singleton site with ring $A$. The global-sections morphism $p_{\mathcal D}$ has structural map given by $A\to\Gamma(\mathcal D,\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})$; its composite with $f$ is $p_{\mathcal C}$ with exactly the scalar action in the statement. Indeed the underlying global sections agree because $f^{-1}$ preserves the terminal sheaf, and the module action is induced by the structural ring map. Apply the unbounded ringed-topos pushforward-composition theorem to $f,p_{\mathcal D}$. Its inverse is $\lambda_E:G_{\mathcal D}RE\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{\mathcal C}E$. This proves Leray for the present general topoi, although the site-formulation of Leray is less general. Define
$$c_{f;K,L}=G_{\mathcal D}(\theta_{K,L})\lambda_E^{-1}.$$
This is a morphism in $D(A)$ and is natural in both arguments since both factors are. The composition theorem computes with K-injective replacements, so this construction imposes no boundedness condition.

source.place: Tag 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition), applied to the punctual topos as in the proof of Tag 0D6H (lemma-Leray-unbounded)

proof.text: Fix $j\in\mathbf Z$ and put $S_Z=\mathcal O_Z[-j]$. The internal-Hom sections model gives natural identifications $H^jG_ZH_Z(K',L')=\operatorname{Hom}(K',L'[j])$. It also gives $H^jG_ZN=\operatorname{Hom}(S_Z,N)$: apply its Hom-complex formula with first argument $\mathcal O_Z$, whose sheaf Hom complex is just the second complex, and shift. Exact restriction to $A$ changes no underlying cocycles or boundaries, hence changes neither identification. The unit complex $\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}$ and each of its shifts are K-flat with flat terms: tensoring with them is the identity or a shift and preserves acyclic complexes. The pullback formula consequently gives $TS_{\mathcal D}=S_{\mathcal C}$ canonically. Moreover $S_Z\otimes^{\mathbf L}N=N[-j]$: in the total tensor only bidegrees $(j,q)$ occur, with differential $(-1)^j d_N$. On these representatives $t_{S_{\mathcal D},N}$ is the same scalar tensor identification, with no permutation of factors. Use the canonical shift comparisons on $T,R$; the cited derived-adjunction shift theorem states that its counit commutes with these comparisons.

Under $H^jG_ZN=\operatorname{Hom}(S_Z,N)$, the map $H^j(\lambda_N^{-1})$ is the canonical adjunction bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}(S_{\mathcal C},N)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(S_{\mathcal D},RN),\qquad a\longmapsto\operatorname{adj}(a).$$
To check this normalization, take a K-injective representative $I$ of $N$ and a K-injective replacement $q:f_*I\to J$. The composition theorem represents $\lambda_N^{-1}$ by the quasi-isomorphism $\Gamma(\mathcal C,I)=\Gamma(\mathcal D,f_*I)\xrightarrow{\Gamma(q)}\Gamma(\mathcal D,J)$. A degree-$j$ cocycle on the left is a chain map $S_{\mathcal C}\to I$. Under the ordinary module adjunction its identical section on $\mathcal D$ is a map $S_{\mathcal D}\to f_*I$; the displayed comparison postcomposes it with $q$. Since $S_{\mathcal D}$ is already K-flat with flat terms, the fraction-representative formula for the derived adjunction says precisely that this represents $\operatorname{adj}(a)$. The Hom-complex model identifies boundaries with homotopies, so the calculation descends to every class, naturally in $N$.

source.place: Tag 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition), representative normalization; Tag 08JA (lemma-section-RHom-over-U); derived adjunction fraction formula

proof.text:
Let $v:K\to L[j]$ correspond to $a:S_{\mathcal C}\to E=H_{\mathcal C}(K,L)$, so $e(a\otimes1_K):K[-j]\to L$ is $v[-j]$. By step 5 its Leray image is $b=\operatorname{adj}(a):S_{\mathcal D}\to RE$, with $\varepsilon_E T(b)=a$. The transpose of $\theta_{K,L}b$ is
$$w=R(e)\mu_{E,K}(b\otimes1_{RK}):S_{\mathcal D}\otimes RK\to RL.$$
Compute its $T\dashv R$ adjunct using naturality of $\varepsilon,t$ and step 2:
$$\varepsilon_L T(w)=e(\varepsilon_E\otimes\varepsilon_K)t_{RE,RK}T(b\otimes1)=e(a\otimes\varepsilon_K)t_{S_{\mathcal D},RK}=v[-j]\,\varepsilon_K[-j].$$
The last equality uses the explicit shifted-unit tensor calculation of step 4. The shift-compatible adjunction and its triangle identity identify the adjunct of $\varepsilon_K[-j]$ with the canonical comparison $RK[-j]\to R(K[-j])$. Hence $w$ is $R(v[-j])$ after that comparison. Rewriting as a map $RK\to RL[j]$ gives exactly $Rv:RK\to R(L[j])\cong(RL)[j]$. The Hom-complex and closed-adjunction identifications in steps 4--5 identify this with $H^j(c_{f;K,L})(v)$. This works for every integer $j$ and every $v$; it uses no isomorphism assertion about $\theta$ or $c$.
